html:
The ongoing "Iran war," as widely referenced in international headlines, and associated developments in critical maritime passages are currently the most significant global development, as the Strait of Hormuz and Bab el-Mandeb are now reportedly under the control of Houthis and Iran, described as an "unprecedented threat." This situation has led to the postponement of a key regional meeting on the Strait of Hormuz and fears for global oil flows, with an Iranian commercial vessel already struck and Saudi Arabia forced to shut down a crucial Red Sea pipeline.

US Foreign Policy & Iran: US President Trump, amidst headlines pointing to an ongoing "Iran war" and his "jaw-dropping bluff" becoming his "worst nightmare," has publicly attributed the attack on the Saudi oil pipeline to Iran. He also urged Ukraine's Zelenskyy to halt strikes on Russian diesel supplies, citing a global shortage, and concluded his visit to Ireland by pledging to remove all Irish whiskey tariffs and reiterating support for Irish unification.

Russia-Ukraine & European Politics: Russia struck a Ukrainian train near the Polish border shortly after Boris Johnson and top European officials departed, which Ukraine and Poland condemned as an "escalation," while Putin warned that sending European troops to Ukraine would mean war with Russia. In Europe, Sweden's election results project a deadlock between left and right blocs, attracting international attention given the far-right anti-immigration Sweden Democrats' potential entry into government, following the Alternative für Deutschland's regional election win in Germany.

BRICS & Global Alignment: The annual BRICS summit, hosted by India with leaders from 28 countries including China and Iran, aimed at countering Western dominance, notably did not condemn the "US-Israel war on Iran," highlighting divisions among member states. A joint declaration from the summit emphasized opposition to unilateral sanctions. Meanwhile, a Saudi defense pact with Turkey and Pakistan has sparked a backlash from the UAE, indicating shifting regional alliances.

Middle East Conflicts: Beyond the critical maritime developments, Israeli attacks on Gaza have resulted in the deaths of over 10 people, including a pregnant woman, with the IDF stating it killed two Hamas engineers. Jordan condemned the storming of Al-Aqsa Mosque by Israeli settlers, while Israeli forces demolished the Mansouri Public School in southern Lebanon and destroyed an extensive Hezbollah tunnel network, which Iran International reports has ignited a blame game in Tehran. In Yemen, government forces, supported by Saudi Arabia, are conducting air attacks to counter a Houthi advance along the Red Sea coast, displacing thousands.

Global Economy & Technology: The debate around artificial intelligence development is intensifying, with US President Trump downplaying warnings of AI risks, citing rivalry with China, while Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei called for 'pacing the frontier' of the AI race due to safety concerns. In economic news, rising fuel prices, underscored by a sarcastic clip shared by Iran's Parliament Speaker Mohammad Bagher Ghalibaf regarding US prices, highlight global energy volatility, further compounded by Uber's departure from key African markets like Nigeria and Uganda.

Other Major Global Events: In other major global developments, an Indonesian passenger ship overturned in the Java Sea, leaving at least 129 people missing, prompting a search operation. Turkish police have detained dozens in raids on gay bars and homes of LGBTQ+ activists, with human rights groups accusing the government of targeting the community. Separately, a newly unveiled statue of rightwing activist Charlie Kirk was vandalized in Phoenix, Arizona, and a San Jose police officer was fired for misusing a license plate tracking system in a domestic abuse case.
